mcq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{For the heat equation with ends at } 0^\circ C, \text{ the appropriate separated solution is:}\)
\(\text{When the ends of a rod are insulated, the boundary conditions are:}\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Wave equation: } \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial x^2}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Boundary conditions: } y(0,t)=0, y(\pi,t)=0.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Initial conditions: } y(x,0)=f(x) \text{ (given), } \frac{\partial y}{\partial t}(x,0)=0.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{General solution: } y(x,t)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin(nx) \cos(nct).\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Fourier sine coefficients: } B_n = \frac{2}{\pi} \left[ \int_0^{\pi/2} x \sin(nx) dx + \int_{\pi/2}^\pi (\pi-x) \sin(nx) dx \right].\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Evaluate integrals: } B_n = \frac{4}{n^2\pi} \sin\left(\frac{n\pi}{2}\right).\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Hence } y(x,t) = \frac{4}{\pi} \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{n^2} \sin\left(\frac{n\pi}{2}\right) \sin(nx) \cos(nct).\)

(1 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{A string of length } \pi \text{ is fixed at both ends. It is initially displaced into the shape } y(x,0) = \begin{cases} x, & 0 \leq x \leq \pi/2 \\ \pi - x, & \pi/2 \leq x \leq \pi \end{cases} \text{ and released from rest. Find the displacement } y(x,t).\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Initial steady state: } u_s(x) = \frac{100}{20}x = 5x.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{New boundary conditions: } u(0,t)=100, u(20,t)=0.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{New steady state: } u_1(x) = \frac{0-100}{20}x + 100 = -5x + 100.\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Let } u(x,t)=u_1(x)+u_2(x,t), \text{ where } u_2 \text{ satisfies heat equation with } u_2(0,t)=0, u_2(20,t)=0.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Initial condition for } u_2: u_2(x,0)=u_s(x)-u_1(x)=5x-(-5x+100)=10x-100.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Solve for } u_2: u_2(x,t)=\sum_{n=1}^\infty B_n \sin\left(\frac{n\pi x}{20}\right) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t/400}.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Fourier sine coefficients: } B_n = \frac{2}{20} \int_0^{20} (10x-100) \sin\left(\frac{n\pi x}{20}\right) dx = \frac{200}{n\pi}[1-(-1)^n].\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Hence } u(x,t) = -5x+100 + \frac{200}{\pi} \sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1-(-1)^n}{n} \sin\left(\frac{n\pi x}{20}\right) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t/400}.\)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{A rod of length 20 cm has its ends kept at } 0^\circ\text{C} \text{ and } 100^\circ\text{C} \text{ until steady state. Then the temperatures at the ends are interchanged. Find the temperature } u(x,t) \text{ after the change.}\)

lq.ANSWER:
Step Marks
\(\text{Initial steady state: \(u_s(x)= \dfrac{100}{l}x.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{After ends insulated: BCs become \(u_x(0,t)=0\), \(u_x(l,t)=0\) (no heat flow).}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{General solution for insulated ends: \(u(x,t)= A_0 + \sum A_n \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t / l^2}.\)}\) (3 Marks)
\(\text{Initial condition: \(u(x,0)= \dfrac{100}{l}x = A_0 + \sum A_n \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right).\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Compute \(A_0 = \dfrac{1}{l} \int_0^l \dfrac{100}{l}x dx = \dfrac{100}{l^2} \cdot \dfrac{l^2}{2} = 50.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{\(A_n = \dfrac{2}{l} \int_0^l \dfrac{100}{l}x \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) dx\) for \(n\geq1.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Evaluate: \(A_n = \dfrac{200}{l^2} \int_0^l x \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) dx = \dfrac{200}{l^2} \left[ \dfrac{l^2}{n^2\pi^2} (\cos(n\pi)-1) \right] = \dfrac{200}{n^2\pi^2} ( (-1)^n - 1 ).\)}\) (3 Marks)
\(\text{Thus \(u(x,t)= 50 + \sum\limits_{n=1}^{\infty} \dfrac{200}{n^2\pi^2}((-1)^n -1) \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2\pi^2 t / l^2}.\)}\) (1 Mark)
lq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{A rod of length $l$ with insulated sides has ends kept at temperatures $0^\circ$ C and $100^\circ$C until steady state.}\\ \text{Then both ends are suddenly insulated. Find the temperature distribution.}\)

lq.ANSWER:
Step Marks
\(\text{Heat equation solution: \(u(x,t)= \sum B_n \sin(nx) e^{-\alpha^2 n^2 t}.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{\(u(x,0)= \sin x + \sin 2x\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(B_1=1\), \(B_2=1\), others zero.}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Thus \(u(x,t)= \sin x e^{-\alpha^2 t} + \sin 2x e^{-4\alpha^2 t}.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Wave equation solution: \(y(x,t)= \sum \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right)\left[C_n \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right)+D_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right)\right].\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{\(y(x,0)= \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right)\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(C_1=1\), others zero. \(y_t(x,0)=0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(D_n=0.\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Thus \(y(x,t)= \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right) \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi c t}{l}\right).\)}\) (2 Marks)
Combine both solutions. (1 Mark)
Discuss physical difference: heat solution decays exponentially, wave solution oscillates indefinitely. (2 Marks)
lq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Solve the heat conduction problem:  $\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} = \alpha^2 \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}$ with boundary conditions  $u(0,t)=0, u(\pi,t)=0,$  and initial condition  $u(x,0)= \sin x + \sin 2x.$}\\ \text{Also solve the wave equation:  $\frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial x^2},$ with $y(0,t)=0, y(l,t)=0, y(x,0)= \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi x}{l}\right), y_t(x,0)=0.$}\)
